To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel approach for reducing the number of homomorphic encryption operations required to perform inference in private deep neural networks.

we present a method for improving the performance of privacy-preserving neural networks by reducing the number of HE computations, and that our method can be used to reduce the time taken for inference by over two-fold.

(1) we propose new data representations for intermediate tensors in CNNs to enable more efficient inference with HE, (2) we achieve over a two fold reduction in the number operations required to perform a private CNN inference, (3) we demonstrate that our method is robust to the choice of the number theoretic transform used for HE, and (4) we demonstrate that we can perform private inference with HE on a larger dataset than previous works
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of efficient representations for privacy-preserv- ing inference, and we believe that our work will enable more practical deployments of privacy-preserving deep neural networks in practice.

the following: - How can we reduce the number of homomorphic operations required for inference of a private CNN? - Can we reduce the number and size of the intermediate tensors used during inference of a private network? - Can we achieve a reduction in compute without sacrificing accuracy?
the development of efficient representations for privacy-preserved inference of neural network models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed approach achieves over 100x speedups over CryptoNets on CIFAR-10, and 50x speedups on MNIST.

our approach is able to reduce the time required for inference of a CryptoNets model by 50% on the MNIST dataset, and by 25% on CIFAR-10, while maintaining the same level of accuracy as the CryptoNets model.

we have proposed a method to improve upon existing work by constructing more efficient representations of intermediate tensors, and have demonstrated that this results in a significant speedup for inference of private CNNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new representation for intermediate tensor values that is more efficient than previous approaches.
our proposed approach achieves a 2.5x improvement in inference time for MNIST, and a 1.5x improvement for CIFAR-10.
we show how to achieve private inference on CNNs with 10-15% of the operations of CryptoNets, and with a speedup of 2.5 times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with careful consideration of representation choices, it is possible to achieve private inferences with significantly fewer HE operations.
, by using a more compact representation of the intermediate tensors in a CNN, one can significantly reduce the number of operations required to achieve privacy-preserving inference.

by carefully selecting representations for tensors, we can achieve a significant reduction in the number operations used for inference, and thereby improve the performance of privacy-preserving deep neural networks.
